title: The Mystery of India's Disappearing Villages
description: Why are villages becoming uninhabited? An evidence-led Hinglish documentary investigating migration, livelihoods and essential services in Uttarakhand. Historical figures are labelled by their source year.

sections.title: Cold Open — The Village That Went Silent
sections.narration: Imagine ek aisa gaon, jahan ghar abhi bhi khade hain. Darwaze abhi bhi lage hain. Raaste abhi bhi wahi hain. Lekin un darwazon ko kholne wala koi nahi. Kabhi yahan subah kheton ki taraf jaate log dikhte honge. Bachchon ki awaazein aati hongi. Shaam ko gharon se roshni nikalti hogi. Aaj, kuch settlements mein, yeh daily rhythm badal chuki hai. Lekin ek khaali ghar dekhkar hum yeh nahi keh sakte ki poora gaon hamesha ke liye chhod diya gaya hai. Humein evidence dekhna hoga. Census 2011 ke records mein India ke 43,324 villages uninhabited record kiye gaye the. Yeh aaj ka live count nahi hai. Lekin yeh ek bada sawaal zaroor khada karta hai. Log apne gaon chhod kyun rahe hain? Kya unhe apna ghar chhodna hai, ya wahan rukna increasingly difficult hota ja raha hai? Is investigation mein hum Uttarakhand ko ek case study ke roop mein dekhenge. Aur jaanenge ki migration, livelihood aur basic services ka connection kya hai.

sections.title: Act 1 — A Country Built on Villages
sections.narration: India ki kahani sirf bade shehron ki kahani nahi hai. Is desh ki zindagi ka ek hissa un gaonon mein bhi basa hai jahan kheti, local markets, families aur traditions ek doosre se judi hoti hain. Jab kisi village ko uninhabited record kiya jaata hai, toh iska ek specific administrative meaning hota hai. Lekin migration ki kahani isse zyada complicated hai. Kuch log kaam ke liye jaate hain. Kuch bachchon ki education ke liye. Kuch medical treatment ke liye. Aur kuch log season ke hisaab se move karte hain. Government ke 2016 Lok Sabha reply mein snow-bound Uttarakhand border areas ke seasonal migration ka zikr hai. Wahan kuch residents winter ke dauraan neeche jaate hain aur spring ke aas-paas wapas lautte hain. Isliye winter mein kisi ghar ka band hona apne aap mein permanent abandonment ka proof nahi. Humein teen cheezein alag rakhni hongi: seasonal absence, temporary migration, aur aisa depopulation jahan settlement uninhabited report hota hai. Census 2011 ne Uttarakhand ke 1,048 uninhabited villages record kiye the. Yeh bhi historical figure hai. Lekin is number ko samajhne ke liye humein state ke baad ke survey ko dekhna hoga. Aur yahin se kahani pahadon ke andar jaati hai.

sections.title: Act 2 — The Himalayan Disappearance
sections.narration: Uttarakhand ki mountains ko aksar postcard ki tarah dekha jaata hai. Lekin yahan rehne ki practical realities har jagah ek jaisi nahi hoti. Uttarakhand ke Rural Development and Migration Commission ki April 2018 report ek specific category record karti hai: 2011 ke baad 734 revenue villages, toks aur majra depopulated list kiye gaye. Yeh report ka historical finding hai, current count nahi. District-wise table mein Pauri Garhwal ka count 186 tha. Bageshwar 77, Pithoragarh 75, Uttarkashi 70 aur Champawat 64 bhi listed the. Map par yeh sirf dots lag sakte hain. Lekin har dot ke peeche ek settlement, ek local history aur kabhi ek family network hota hai. Phir bhi humein careful rehna hai. Survey ka term aur definition samajhna zaroori hai. Kya village permanently empty tha? Kya kuch households seasonally absent the? Kya baad mein koi wapas aaya? Yeh questions original survey ko dekhkar hi fully resolve honge. Jo evidence abhi humein milta hai, woh ek serious pattern suggest karta hai. Lekin pattern ko samajhne ke liye sirf map kaafi nahi. Humein poochna hoga ki logon ke saamne kaun se options the. Aur un options mein employment ka role kitna bada tha?

sections.title: Act 2 — The Economics of Leaving
sections.narration: Kisi ghar ko chhodna aasaan nahi hota. Lekin rukna bhi mushkil ho sakta hai. Agar local employment limited ho, toh young adults ko kaam ke liye doosri jagah jaana pad sakta hai. Agar higher education door ho, toh students aur families move karne ka decision le sakte hain. Agar medical care tak pahunch mushkil ho, toh daily life aur uncertain ho sakti hai. Commission ki apni 2018 report mein livelihood aur employment ki problem sabse bada listed migration reason hai. Table mein iska share 50.16 percent diya gaya hai. Yeh gram-panchayat-level survey ka reported reason share hai, individual migrant ke har case ka explanation nahi. Education aur health facilities ki kami bhi table mein alag reasons ke roop mein listed hain. Ek aur detail migration ko samajhne mein madad karti hai. Commission ke destination table mein 19.46 percent nearby towns, 15.18 percent district headquarters aur 35.69 percent state ke doosre districts listed hain. In teen shares ko jodne par 70.33 percent banta hai—yaani roughly 70 percent reported destinations state ke andar the. Yaani har migrant ne Uttarakhand ko permanently alvida nahi kaha. Kai log nearby towns, district headquarters ya doosre districts ki taraf gaye. Gaon unka home reh sakta hai, lekin rozgaar aur services ki wajah se unki daily life kahin aur shift ho jaati hai. Isliye migration ko sirf emotional attachment ke scale par judge karna unfair hoga. Kabhi-kabhi yeh family ke future ka practical decision hota hai. Lekin jab bahut se log ek hi direction mein move karte hain, toh gaon mein peeche reh jaane walon ki zindagi bhi badalti hai.

sections.title: Act 2 — When Essential Services Disappear
sections.narration: Ek gaon tab khaali nahi hota jab aakhri insaan chala jaata hai. Kabhi-kabhi woh tab khaali hone lagta hai jab roz ki zindagi mushkil hoti chali jaati hai. Ek road, ek health centre, peene ka paani aur reliable electricity—yeh sab daily life ka foundation hain. Commission ki 2018 report migration ke reasons ko alag-alag categories mein rakhti hai. Education facilities ki kami 15.21 percent listed hai. Health facilities ki kami 8.83 percent. Roads, electricity, water aur doosre infrastructure ki kami 3.74 percent. Agricultural land ki productivity ya yield mein kami 5.44 percent. Aur wild animals se crops ko nuksaan 5.61 percent. Yeh shares survey ke reported migration reasons hain; inhe villages ke percentage ya har household ke experience ke roop mein nahi padhna chahiye. Pahadi farming mein terrain, irrigation, rainfall aur crop protection jaise challenges ho sakte hain. Lekin inmein se kisi ek factor ko har village ke empty hone ka single cause kehna evidence se aage jaana hoga. Humein ek connected system dekhna hoga. Jab livelihoods limited hon aur services tak pahunch mushkil ho, migration attractive ho sakti hai. Aur jab population kam hoti hai, toh farming aur local community networks par bhi pressure badh sakta hai. Ab hum is cycle ke centre par pahunch rahe hain.

sections.title: Act 2 — The Big Reveal: It Is Not One Cause
sections.narration: Ab tak humne alag-alag reasons dekhe. Employment. Education. Healthcare. Roads. Water. Agriculture. Lekin in sabko ek saath rakhne par picture badal jaati hai. Village depopulation ko ek single villain se explain nahi kiya ja sakta. Yeh pressures ek doosre se connected ho sakte hain. Agar local jobs kam hain, young people move karte hain. Agar population kam hoti hai, toh farms aur local businesses ko chalana mushkil ho sakta hai. Agar services tak access difficult hai, toh families ke liye wapas settle hona aur complicated ho sakta hai. Yeh ek possible reinforcing cycle hai—har village mein same sequence prove nahi hua, lekin available report ke patterns is relationship ko investigate karne ki wajah dete hain. National migration data bhi ek caution deta hai. PLFS 2020-21 ne India ki overall migration rate 28.9 percent estimate ki. Lekin migration rate ka matlab abandoned villages ka percentage nahi hai. Migration ke reasons aur routes bahut diverse hain. Published stream data rural-to-rural movement bhi dikhata hai. Kuch migration seasonal hota hai. Kuch circular. Kuch permanent. Isliye ek winter mein band ghar ko ghost village keh dena misleading ho sakta hai. [PAUSE 0.8s] Yahi is investigation ka big reveal hai: gaon sirf isliye disappear nahi hote ki log apni roots bhool jaate hain. Kabhi-kabhi livelihoods, services, geography aur aspirations milkar aisi conditions banate hain jahan move karna practical choice ban jaata hai. Lekin ek fair question ab bhi baaki hai. Kya migration hamesha tragedy hoti hai?

sections.title: Act 3 — Can a Village Come Back?
sections.narration: Ab ek counter-argument ko honestly dekhna zaroori hai. Kya migration hamesha buri cheez hai? Nahi. Kisi young person ke liye city jaana better education ka chance ho sakta hai. Kisi family ke liye stable employment aur healthcare access ka raasta. Migrants apne ghar par paise bhej sakte hain. Aur kuch log season ke hisaab se move karke wapas aate hain. Isliye har migrant ko ek tragic figure ki tarah dikhana unfair hoga. Har village ko uski historical population tak wapas le jaana bhi zaroori ya practical nahi hota. Lekin is argument ka doosra hissa bhi hai. Kya kisi insaan ke paas apne gaon mein rehne ka real option hona chahiye? Government ka Border Area Development Programme remote border areas mein roads, water, education, health aur skill development jaise infrastructure areas ko support karne ke liye describe kiya gaya hai. Programme ka hona apne aap mein yeh prove nahi karta ki har village ki problem solve ho gayi. Outcomes ko village-level evidence se check karna padega. Sirf road bana dena enough nahi agar local livelihood sustainable nahi. Sirf school hona enough nahi agar quality education tak access nahi. Aur sirf logon ko wapas bula lena enough nahi agar unke paas income aur services nahi. Isliye solution ka focus return migration ko force karna nahi hona chahiye. Focus hona chahiye choice par. Jo jaana chahe, woh ja sake. Jo rehna chahe, uske paas bhi ek viable future ho. Aur jo wapas aana chahe, uske liye bhi basic conditions hon. Is decision ko samajhne ke liye migration ko sirf loss ya success ke label mein fit nahi kar sakte. Ek household ke liye income badh sakti hai, lekin usi waqt elderly parents ke liye care ka arrangement mushkil ho sakta hai. Ek student ko better college mil sakta hai, lekin family ka local support network door ho sakta hai. Yeh outcomes har family ke liye same nahi hote. Isliye policy aur storytelling dono ko individual experiences aur local data ke beech farq rakhna chahiye. Local planning ko bhi village ke context mein dekhna hoga. Har district ki geography, access aur economy alag hai. Ek hi scheme ya ek hi solution sab jagah kaam kare, yeh maan lena sahi nahi. Isliye local residents ki priorities, transparent data aur long-term maintenance ko decision ka hissa banana zaroori hai.

sections.title: Closing — The Door That Remains
sections.narration: Wapas us darwaze par aate hain. Ek khaali ghar bhi kabhi kisi ka poora jahaan hua karta tha. Us aangan mein kabhi zindagi thi. Ho sakta hai kisi ke liye woh ghar aaj bhi home ho, chahe woh kahin aur kaam karta ho. Aur ho sakta hai kuch settlements waqai permanently uninhabited ho chuki hon. Evidence ko in dono realities mein farq karna hoga. India ke disappearing villages ki story sirf logon ke jaane ki story nahi. Yeh un choices ki story hai jo logon ke saamne hoti hain. Asli sawaal yeh nahi ki har koi wapas aayega ya nahi. Sawaal yeh hai: kya hum aisa future bana sakte hain jahan kisi ko apna ghar chhodna majboori na lage—and jahan kisi ka jaana bhi uski apni choice ho?
